# Material interdependency report

World Design Rule 007 (Automated Compliance, register entry WDR-007-C): material and profession coverage generated from the recipe data and the job code, checked against Rules 001 (every standard crafting material consumed by at least 3 meaningfully different recipes across at least 2 professions), 002 (every production profession supplies another) and 003 (near-duplicate recipes count once). Run `python3 tools/check_materials.py` to check and `--write` to regenerate; `--strict` also fails on open violations. Exceptions are recorded in `docs/systems/material_exceptions.json`.

## How it is counted

- **Standard crafting material:** an item of type `resource` (items.json) that a recipe or a construction consumes. Food, medicine and equipment that a recipe also takes are end goods (listed below, not held to Rule 001).
- **Meaningful uses:** the distinct products of the recipes consuming it (Rule 003: two recipes making the same item count once) plus the distinct kinds of construction consuming it. Construction counts because Rule 001's own example counts a house: `house_cost`, `workshop_cost` (all kinds as one), the loft, the storefront and the shop fittings (`shop_equipment`) are five construction uses (balance.json).
- **Profession of a recipe:** the NPC job whose work code runs it (tools/check_materials.py `JOB_WORK`, cited functions checked). The game has no recipe-to-trade field and the station does not decide it (the workbench serves the tanner and the carpenter). Recipes no job runs are the player's alone and add no profession; households (home work, their own houses) are not a profession, and the game has no builder trade, so construction adds uses but no profession.
- **Supplying (Rule 002):** a production profession (one that runs a recipe or harvests a node) supplies another when one of its products is an input of a recipe that profession runs, an item it buys for its trade (`NPCBrain.BUYS`) or an item it keeps for its work, such as its tools (`NPCBrain.KEEPS`). Merchants' purchases are resale: shown, not counted.
- **Orphaned recipe:** makes nothing that a recipe or construction consumes, a job needs, or that is an end good (food, medicine, equipment, a cart, a plant, or an item with a code-defined use in resources.json).
